title: Choose Keel's visual world
question: This look carries the landing page and the whole app. Keep the lead direction, take an alternate, or re-roll for a fresh hand.

options.label: Security Paper
options.lineage: banknote, cheque and stock-certificate security printing
options.thesis: Every number printed like money: exact, serial-numbered, tamper-evident.
options.viewport: One certificate sheet: headline and a working broker-file drop on the left, a guilloche rosette engraved from your equity curve on the right with net P&L as its denomination, and a MICR line of stats along the foot.
options.risk: Fussy engraving would read as a 1950s bank; the pattern must stay behind the numbers.

raised.raise: Two plates, strictly: guilloche and microprint sit on the back plate, and every number and control prints on the front plate, never inside the pattern.
Every risk view has a hard floor: daily-loss and max-drawdown limits print as a line the equity run stops above, with named states (clear, near, breached).
Meaning through pattern, not hue: gains print solid, losses print hatched, so P&L reads without colour.
A serial spine: every trade, session and report carries a serial number, and the numbered spine is how you navigate.
Registered plates: one fixed keyline grid, with fills, stops and notes printing in register on it.

options.label: Trading Floor
options.lineage: open-outcry pits: trading jackets, badges and paper order tickets
options.thesis: Every trade is a ticket you file and stamp; Keel does the filing.
options.viewport: Jacket-gold ground, a giant trader badge, a fanned stack of sample order tickets with one stamped RULE BROKEN, and a ticket-slot file drop.
options.risk: The most familiar move: trading imagery for a trading product, and the pit era can read as nostalgia.

options.label: Darkroom
options.thesis: Develop your edge: trades move through fixed stations, and test strips are backtests.
options.viewport: An amber room, 'Develop your edge.' in grease pencil, an equity curve emerging in the developer tray, and a test strip of five stop sizes beneath it.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: stations map the improvement loop and test strips map backtesting. Loses on audience fit: traders don't live in darkrooms.
options.risk: All-amber fights red/green P&L and is hard on long data sessions.

options.label: Glaze Shelf
options.thesis: Each strategy a glazed cup, its drawdown running toward the shelf of your loss limit.
options.viewport: A shelf of strategies, each glaze run stopping above its limit line.
options.case: Vivid for prop-firm drawdown, but ceramics is foreign to traders and only one module maps.
options.kept: Every risk view has a hard floor with named states.
options.risk: A metaphor that explains one page and confuses the rest.

options.label: Block Registration
options.thesis: A trade built up in registered layers: the price keyline first, then fills, stops and notes.
options.viewport: A price line printed alone, then fills and stops dropping into register.
options.case: The layered reveal suits trade review, but the print tradition is decoration here, not a trader's world.
options.kept: One fixed keyline grid with each data layer in register.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: The journal as an early desktop: trades open as windows on one plane.
options.viewport: Overlapping windows: trade log, calendar and a chart in dithered grey.
options.case: Works as an interface, but traders don't identify with it, and two tones flatten P&L.
options.kept: Meaning through pattern: gains solid, losses hatched.
options.risk: Retro novelty that wears off by week two.

options.label: Tape J-Card
options.thesis: Your month as a hand-numbered tape, sessions listed down the spine.
options.viewport: An unfolding card with sessions numbered down the spine.
options.case: Lo-fi bedroom craft undercuts a tool about exact numbers.
options.kept: A serial spine you navigate by.
options.risk: Reads as a zine, not a financial record.

options.label: Multiplane Dawn
options.thesis: Your trading history as painted depth planes: today nearest, years behind.
options.viewport: The camera sinks through layered planes toward today's session.
options.case: Traders don't see themselves in a painted forest, and parallax hides numbers.
options.kept: Ornament behind, every number on the front plate.
options.risk: Pretty, but slow to read and wrong for dense tables.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark SaaS product page trading journals ship, done with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A centred headline and two buttons over a large dashboard screenshot.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other trading journals, by design.
